## What

The Queue's "**N waiting on you**" headline (`QueueSummary.waitingOnYou` =
`tierCounts.decision`) once showed **7060+** when the real owner-decision count
was **~40**. The number even grew over time. It was not backlog — it was a
counting failure with a structural root cause.

Root cause: the placement watchdog (`pot/placement-watchdog.ts`) opens a
durable **blocker** escalation for every cursed placement ("Cursed placement:
F-X failed 301× — stopped auto-re-placing"), from owner
`system:pot-placement-watchdog`, **with no options**. The fleet curses
thousands of placements; ~7218 such escalations were opened and only ~135 ever
resolved. The attention reader (`agent-tools/plans/attention.ts`, source #2)
mapped **every open blocker escalation to the `decision` tier** — no cap, no
sender filter, no rollup — so all ~7083 open ones counted as "waiting on you".
The same was true of `green-checkpoint`/cup operational escalations.

## Why it's the wrong shape

An operational escalation ("X is cursed / stuck / not green") is an **alert** —
something to surface, not a decision-with-choice the owner must make. It is also
a **redundant duplicate of a derived health metric**: cursed placements are
already counted as `SystemHealth.placements.cursed` (`system-health/compute.ts`),
which is the live source of truth. So a per-placement durable escalation is
un-GC'd noise duplicating a number the system already derives.

## The fix (queue-pending-accuracy-and-drift-2026-06-16)

1. **Tier it right.** `coordEscalationToAttention` now calls the shared
   `isOperationalEscalation(from, hasOptions)` — a `system`/`system:*` sender
   **with no options** is `alert`, never `decision`. Genuine decisions come
   from agents (`coord:escalate` / `coord:ask-owner`) and carry a real sender or
   options. (One reader change demotes the existing flood AND future ones.)
2. **GC it.** `attention/reconcile-escalations.ts` is an hourly sweep
   (`dbos/periodic-workflows.ts`) that auto-resolves operational escalations
   idle past a TTL (`OPERATIONAL_ESCALATION_TTL_MS`, default 48h — lowered from 3d per infra-perf-robustness-audit-2026-06-18 D-005; reconcile-escalations.ts:40) — batch-limited
   so a large backlog drains over several ticks. Genuine (non-system / with
   options) escalations are **never** auto-resolved.
3. **Stop minting blockers.** The watchdog now emits the cursed-placement
   escalation as `advisory`, not `blocker` (it has already stopped re-placing —
   it is informing, not blocked).

## The invariant (derive-don't-store) — hold this for every new attention source

The queue is a **projection of live state**, not a hand-maintained pile. An item
is "pending" **iff its source is still open**, and resolution flows through the
source's own verb (`plans:set-status`, `coord:resolve`, `conversations:answer`,
`issues:close`). When you add an attention source:

- **Never** put a high-volume, automated, option-less signal in the `decision`
  tier. If it has no choice for the human, it is an `alert` at most.
- If a signal is **already a derived metric** (health panel, a count), do not
  also mint a durable per-item escalation/issue for it — that double-counts and
  drifts. Surface the rollup, link to detail.
- If a source can accumulate without a human acting (escalations, issues), it
  **must** have a reconciliation/TTL path so the projection self-heals without
  relying on any agent remembering to resolve it. Prompts will not hold.

Counterpart fleet-health signal worth its own look: ~7000 cursed placements is a
real work-item-quality problem (ill-specified items / wedging cups), independent
of the queue.
